questions.question: When using the simulator, what does clicking the “Tritanopia” button do?

answers.a: Displays how someone with green-color blindness sees the image
answers.b: Displays how someone with blue-color blindness sees the image
answers.c: Displays how the image would look in grayscale
answers.d: Displays how someone with normal color vision sees the image

explanations.a: This is incorrect. Deuteranopia affects green perception, not blue. Tritanopia is related to blue-color blindness.
explanations.b: Correct! This image shows how the given image appears to someone with Tritanopia (blue-color blindness).
explanations.c: This option is incorrect. Total color blindness (monochromacy) would show the image in shades of gray.
explanations.d: This option is incorrect because the image represents Tritanopia, not normal color vision.

questions.question: Which of the following properties is associated with total color blindness (achromatopsia)?

answers.a: Complete inability to perceive any colors, only shades of gray
answers.b: Difficulty distinguishing between specific colors, such as red and green
answers.c: Normal color vision but reduced clarity of vision
answers.d: Enhanced ability to see colors in dim lighting

explanations.a: Correct! Total color blindness (achromatopsia) means the complete inability to perceive colors, resulting in a grayscale view of the world.
explanations.b: Incorrect. This describes partial color blindness, such as Deuteranopia or Protonopia, not total color blindness.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Reduced clarity of vision may sometimes accompany achromatopsia, but this is not the defining characteristic.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Achromatopsia does not enhance color perception in dim lighting; it eliminates color perception altogether.
